title: Finite-energy Gaussian Bobkov inequality
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be infinitely continuously differentiable, take values in $[0,1]$, and have each coordinate partial derivative in Gaussian $L^2$. Write $\nabla_G f(x)=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (\partial_i f(x))^2}$, and let $U$ denote the Gaussian profile that equals the Gaussian density at the Gaussian quantile for inputs in $(0,1)$ and is zero otherwise. Then
\[
U\!\left(\int f\,d\gamma_n\right)\le \int \sqrt{U(f(x))^2+\nabla_G f(x)^2}\,d\gamma_n(x),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
hypotheses_covered: Each coordinate partial derivative of $f$ belongs to Gaussian $L^2$
